text: The Battle of the Nations is an international historical medieval battles world championship first held in 2010 at the Khotyn Fortress in Ukraine, with its origins tracing back to a meeting of national team captains in Kharkiv, Ukraine in 2009. It is a full-contact competition using metal weapons and follows a standardized set of unified international rules specifically developed for the event, replacing prior variations in national historical medieval battle (HMB) rules. National teams compete in various events, all of which are full contact, with no stage reenactment battles included. Each national team must consist of between 8 and 50 fighters, composed of representatives from historical medieval battle clubs or individual fighters who have undergone a conventional national selection process. Teams from up to 60 countries have participated. The event has been held annually in Europe in April until the 2020 and 2021 tournaments were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and again in 2022 due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The tradition stems from Russia, where large-scale full-contact battles with historically accurate armor, heraldry, and weapons have long been held in historical sites. While heraldry used in the competition reflects modern teams, the combatants represent armored fighters from the 12th to 15th centuries. The event features multiple combat formats, including individual duels, 5vs5 group battles, and 21vs21 mass battles, with archery also included. Over 25,000 spectators attend annually. The first tournament in 2010 featured Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, and Poland, with Russia winning most categories. In 2011, seven teams participated, including Italy, Germany, and Team Quebec (Ost du Quebec), the first non-European team, which sent a team of nine fighters and three support staff from Montreal. The US entered for the first time in 2012, with members from the Society for Creative Anachronism, forming a cross-group association. The 2012 event included 12 countries, increasing to 22 by 2013, which was held in Aigues-Mortes, France—marking the first time the event took place outside Eastern Europe. The 2014 event occurred in Trogir, Croatia, and introduced the first female official nomination in the fencing "Triathlon" category. In 2015, the women's buhurt "all vs all" category was promoted as the year's innovation. The event has seen participation from numerous countries, including Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Czech Republic, Japan, Luxembourg, New Zealand, Spain, and the UK, with fighters from Portugal also attending and fighting with the Luxembourg team. The full standings for each year reflect consistent dominance by Russian teams in most categories, with notable performances by France, Ukraine, Poland, Belarus, and other nations. The competition has evolved over time, adding new categories such as "professional fights" and "all vs all," and expanding in scale and geographic reach.

Countries and even different regions within one country agreed upon a set of unified international rules for the conduct of battles. The first "Battle of the Nations" event took place in 2010 at the Khotyn Fortress in Ukraine and featured national teams from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, and Poland; Russia won the most first-place positions. The event included three categories: a duel (1 vs 1), group battles (5 vs 5), and mass battles (21 vs 21). Non-members who came to support the teams participated in non-security buhurts. The second event in 2011 also occurred at the Khotyn Fortress, with seven national teams participating—adding the "professional fight" and "all vs all" categories; the latter allowed non-national team members to fight for their countries. Russia again won the first places. The festival attracted about 30,000 spectators, and a documentary about the participants' lives was produced. The 2012 event, the third, was held in Warsaw, Poland, and included representatives from twelve countries; it introduced mounted knight battles into the traditionally on-foot HMB world championship for the first time. The top four teams were Russia, Ukraine, Poland, and the USA. The 2013 event, the fourth, was held in Aigues-Mortes, France, with twenty-two teams from Europe, the Americas, and the Pacific Rim; due to the increased number of teams, the "pro rules" fights and mounted jousting were removed from the main arena. The top four teams were Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, and the USA. In 2014, due to dissatisfaction with the HMBIA, some member states formed the International Medieval Combat Federation. The 2014 event, the fifth, was held in Trogir, Croatia, with around 30 countries expected. The 2015 event, the sixth, took place in Prague. The 2016 event, the seventh, was also held in Prague, with 35 countries expected. The 2017 event, the eighth, was held in Barcelona, Spain, and marked the first year that Chinese, Brazilian, and Turkish teams joined. The 2018 event, the ninth, was held in Rome, Italy. The 2019 event, the tenth, was held in the Smederevo Fortress, Serbia. The 2020 and 2021 events were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and the 2022 tournament was cancelled due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine. For the 10th anniversary in 2019, the HMBIA introduced the 150 vs 150 category, a unique mass-battle event where alliances from the 30vs30 category compete in the largest mass battle ever offered. The valid battle categories for national team competitions in HMB include the duel (1 vs 1), group battles (5 vs 5), mass battles (21 vs 21), and the 150 vs 150 category. Valid non-battle categories also exist.
